title: Collaborative entrepreneurship: transparency, shared risk and meritocracy as the base of workplace trust
summary: Cris Pop recaps a Thunder Talks session with RebelDot's Tudor Ciulean and adds his own view on company culture. The core idea: transparency builds trust, trust builds ownership, and open, meritocratic teams beat "factory culture" companies.

principles.text: Work with people, not for them: share the weight of uncertainty and treat their wins and struggles as yours.
principles.quote: Because when you work with someone, you share the weight of uncertainty. Their wins feel like your wins. Their struggles become your struggles.

principles.text: Lasting business relationships are forged in uncomfortable honesty, not polite half-truths.
principles.quote: Not the easy kind. The vulnerable kind. The kind that risks rejection in order to invite trust.

principles.text: Transparency creates a chain: trust, then ownership, then care and creativity.
principles.quote: Transparency builds trust. Trust fuels ownership. Ownership generates care and sparks creativity.

principles.text: Tell people the real situation, even when it is bad, instead of making false promises, and let them choose to stay or go.
principles.quote: Instead of making false promises, he kept everyone informed about the reality they were facing together.

principles.text: Avoid factory culture that makes people interchangeable; build a meritocracy where the best idea wins regardless of title.
principles.quote: It's built on a meritocratic foundation where the best ideas win, regardless of who suggests them. It doesn't matter if you're the CEO or the newest hire.

principles.text: Give people the why, not just the how; shared understanding of purpose beats a perfect strategy.
principles.quote: Most companies do the opposite. They hide the struggles, micromanage the process, and wonder why people seem disengaged.
